static_traits.name: Chen Yu
static_traits.family_status: Originally from London; now lives in Vienna, Austria
static_traits.social_status: Having a best friend to confide relationship problems in
static_traits.medical_history: No similar psychological problems or treatment before; no significant physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, good logic, highly cooperative, able to do self-Reflection and evidence examination; calm tone

basic_info.main_problem: I am constantly afraid my boyfriend no longer loves me, although we have been together for 5 years.
basic_info.core_demands: I realize this fear is affecting my mental health and our relationship, so I am seeking counseling to resolve this fear.

core_beliefs: I will be abandoned by my partner

special_situations.event: When we should be spending the evening together, my boyfriend is still focused on Work
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If he chooses Work during our time together, it means he does not love me and the relationship is deteriorating
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Strongly focuses on whether he provides companionship, repeatedly communicates with him and requests more verbal expression to obtain confirmation

special_situations.event: Boyfriend saying he wants to be alone, needing Being alone
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If he chooses Being alone, he is distancing himself from me and preparing to leave me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Talking with him again to express my worries and needs, seeking reassurance to ease unease
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: He is going to leave me

special_situations.event: Boyfriend saying 'I love you' markedly less often
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Love must be proven through frequent verbal affirmation; if he does not say it often, it means he no longer loves me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Directly asks for more verbal affirmation, repeatedly confirms whether he loves me

special_situations.event: Boyfriend sometimes choosing Work instead of spending time with me
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If he does not prioritize me, it means I am not important to him and he does not love me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignores evidence of him expressing care in other ways, continuing to focus on negative cues to seek certainty
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not important to him

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be loved and affirmed stably and explicitly (especially verbal 'I love you')
core_conflict.fear: Fearing Being rejected and abandonment, worrying the intimate relationship will suddenly be lost
defense_goal: Maintaining relationship security and reducing the risk of abandonment by constantly seeking verbal reassurance and companionship

object_relations.self_representation: A partner feeling unloved and unsafe in the relationship
object_relations.object_representation: A cold/distant partner, preoccupied with work, with little verbal expression

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor asks for evidence and challenges the thought 'he does not love me / will leave me', or discusses the boyfriend being busy and saying 'I love you' less
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client tends to interpret the other's Silence and busyness as rejection and distance (transference: projecting inner unease onto the other's intentions)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Repeatedly emphasizing 'he does not love me' in an anxious, evidence-seeking tone, asking for confirmation and comfort; when challenged, giving superficial Rationalization Interpretations but returning to the worrying theme.

manifestations: Strongly relying on the other's verbal affirmation in the intimate relationship to counter Loneliness and insecurity
When the boyfriend is busy with Work or chooses Being alone, markedly triggering Loneliness and the experience of being ignored
outcomes: Rising Relationship tension and communication stress
Evening Anxiety worsened, Daily life disrupted

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Treating 'love requires frequent verbal affirmation' as a rigid standard for relationships
Tends to measure intimacy and security by 'he should say I love you more often'

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Repeatedly worrying about the relationship, cautiously seeking evidence, but still struggling to let go of Anxiety
Worrying things will not change even after communicating, thus continuously monitoring the other's expressions and behaviors

positive_force: The partner is still considerate and thoughtful on a nonverbal level (attention and care still exist)
Has a best friend who can provide emotional support and a channel to confide in
Willing to proactively seek professional help and cooperate with exercises such as recording and evidence examination
Able to Identify automatic thoughts and consider alternative Interpretations (some cognitive flexibility present)
negative_force: Over-relies on external verbal affirmation (External Validation) as the only proof of love
Cognitive distortion: Jumping to Conclusions/Mind Reading
Low tolerance for uncertainty, marked evening Anxiety
Ongoing worry causing impaired attention, Decline in work performance and worsening Relationship tension

target_behavior.behavior: Relationship Anxiety and repeated worries that 'my partner does not love me / will leave me'
antecedent: More easily triggered when spending evenings with partner
Partner busy with work, less companionship
Partner says 'I love you' less often
target_behavior.core_reason: Treats verbal affirmation as the core standard of love and relationship security, relying on external validation; cognitive biases of 'Jumping to Conclusions / Mind Reading' exist.
target_behavior.function: Seeking comfort and reassurance to gain security and maintain intimacy; escaping uncertainty and Loneliness
target_behavior.consequence: Decline in work performance, Relationship tension, impaired attention, Daily life affected
